extracted.subtask_description: Creating short, deadpan, news-style headlines in the voice of The Onion using a headline-first workflow and templates (Area Man, Study Finds, Sources Confirm, etc.). Emphasizes volume, individual ideation, and craft rules so a signed-off headline can be plausibly expanded into a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline-First Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories begin as headlines. Once a headline is signed off, writers craft a story to match. (Opposite of real newsrooms.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The headline is the starting point and must be approved before a full story is written; write headlines strong enough to carry the piece and guide how the body will be constructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume Funnel (pitch and selection metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: 500 headlines pitched every week; ~12 selected for publication; 60–70% killed in an hour during pre-meeting; each writer required to bring ~15 headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes high-volume ideation: success relies on generating many ideas and quickly filtering. Expect most ideas to be discarded; persistence and quotas matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brainstorming Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Everybody apart first — individual ideation in their own space. Short pre-meeting separates 'gems from garbage.' Main session refines surviving headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a staged process: ideate alone to produce raw quantity, use a short triage to remove weak items, then collaboratively refine the best headlines. The pre-meeting accelerates filtering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and Style (AP, matter-of-fact, deadpan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter-of-fact AP-news style. Mimic real journalism conventions exactly. The earnest, deadpan tone IS the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the conventions of straight news writing (AP style, formal register, neutral reporting). Avoid melodramatic or overtly jokey wording; the humor comes from treating absurdity with journalistic earnestness.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Saying Exactly What the Person Is Thinking" (write in character)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in character. Force them to write completely honestly. The unspoken truth becomes the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invent the internal, embarrassing, or taboo thought the subject would have and state it plainly in news framing. The laugh comes from exposing the private truth as if it were public fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-Substitution Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Take serious news framing. Change a key word or two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from legitimate headline constructions and swap in a word or two to subvert the meaning. Examples in practice: 'Nation's Senators Carefully Avoid …' or 'Area Man Realizes…'. Small changes that alter implications are often most effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Onion Templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated headline templates include: 'Area Man / Area Woman'; 'Nation Reflects on…'; 'Sources Confirm…'; 'Study Finds…'; 'Local…'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these structural templates as proven scaffolds: 'Area Man' universalizes an everyman; 'Nation Reflects' channels collective inner monologue; 'Sources Confirm' lampoons sourcing conventions; 'Study Finds' parodies research headlines; 'Local' lets absurdity be hyperlocal. Plug honest or absurd specifics into these molds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it sound like a real news headline (AP style)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it sound like a real news headline (AP style)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The headline should convincingly mimic legitimate news copy so the reader initially accepts its register; if it doesn't pass as a real headline, the deadpan effect is weakened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it reveal an uncomfortable truth nobody says aloud?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it reveal an uncomfortable truth nobody says aloud?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best headlines expose an honest, awkward, or taboo thought. Check whether the line surfaces a truth people recognize but avoid stating publicly—that recognition is the source of the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a specific subject (Area Man, Local Mom)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a specific subject (Area Man, Local Mom)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines should usually attach to a relatable, concrete subject to ground the absurdity. Using archetypal figures ('Area Man') or specific local types focuses the reader and makes the premise easier to expand into a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is it deadpan-funny without overt jokes?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it deadpan-funny without overt jokes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid punchlines that read like stand-up one-liners or overtly jokey phrasing. The humor should arise from the mismatch between the serious tone and the underlying absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Could the body of the article extend the premise plausibly?
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the body of the article extend the premise plausibly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before approving a headline, ensure there is enough concrete, funny detail to write a full piece that follows the headline's premise. If you can't imagine a plausible article that supports the joke, the headline may be too thin.
